java_diagnostic.interpretation: 85% is strong and changes the risk picture: the 'cold since Dec 2025' worry was too broad. Concurrency/JVM, Spring and JPA/Hibernate are all perfect — the framework-level knowledge he actually used daily at Onextel held up completely. The real softness is narrower: Java Core (60%) and Collections (75%), i.e. base-language mechanics and collections internals specifically. That is exactly W2's Saturday topic ('Java: collections internals, generics, Streams') — already correctly targeted, no redesign needed. No change to the Java thread's weight or schedule; this just confirms the plan was aimed right.

warmup_result.idiom_verdict: STRONGER than the diagnostic implied. Unprompted he reached for re.findall(r'\b\w+\b', text.lower()) to tokenize and case-fold in one line, collections.Counter to tally, max(counts.values()) for the top frequency, a generator expression with min() for the alphabetical tie-break, and an empty-input guard most candidates skip. That is genuine Python instinct, not hand-rolled Java-shaped loops. Revise the earlier 'fluency gap' read downward.
bugs: Line 9: `if counts == max_counts` compares the Counter object to an int — always False, so the generator is empty and min() raises ValueError on EVERY non-empty input. Should be `count`.
Line 6: `return none` — lowercase; Python has no `none`, so empty input raises NameError. Should be `None`.
warmup_result.verified_behaviour: Ran it: 'the cat the dog THE bird. cat!' -> ValueError; 'b a b a' -> ValueError; '' -> NameError. The function fails 100% of the time despite being algorithmically correct.
warmup_result.the_real_finding: He does not run his code. Both bugs die on the first execution and both are single-token slips (counts/count, none/None) — no amount of Python knowledge catches them, and one run catches both. This is the highest-leverage habit to fix, and it is worth naming that he is an SDET by trade. In a live proctored round an untested solution that looks right but throws is simply a fail. Training target for W1-6 is the verify loop (run it, or dry-run one input aloud, before calling it done) — NOT more Python theory.
warmup_result.still_needed: His honest timing for the attempt, and the fix made by HIM (bugs were pointed out by class, not corrected for him).
